correctness.rationale: For b=1, exact reciprocal comparison forces z_n<=1/(q n+z0^{-1}) and y_{n+1}<=a z_n. Exact ratio y_n/z_n gives a quadratic expansion y_n=a z_n+d z_n^2+O(z_n^3). Taylor expansion of the exact inverse recurrence gives u_{n+1}-u_n=c+k z_n+O(z_n^2), c>0. Summing first yields u_n=c n+O(log n) and z_n=1/(cn)+O(logn/n^2); both the latter error and z_n^2 are summable, proving the finite-part limit. Exact rational coefficient identities and three finite numerical orbits are verified in verify.py; finite tests are not used as proof.
